subject: Token split, tool/system attribution and billing rounding — POC cost modeling

From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Token counting & rounding for hosted API — POC cost modeling

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to move to a short POC (2–3 weeks) to validate latency and cost. Before we start I need to model expected monthly costs so procurement can sign off. A few specific questions we couldn't get answered on the call: 

1) For a single generation request where we send a system prompt (30 tokens), user prompt (120 tokens), and receive a model response (approx. 240 tokens), how are tokens counted on the hosted rate card? Are system tokens always billed as input?

2) We plan to use function/tool calls (external lookup service). If the model triggers a tool call and the tool returns 400 tokens which we then re-feed into the model for a short follow-up, how are those tool-produced tokens attributed across requests? Do you charge for the tool output when it is first created, or only when the model consumes it?

3) Streaming — we will stream responses to the client. Is the output token count determined by the final full completion, or aggregated per-stream-chunk? Any rounding rules for streaming?

4) Rounding — we saw references to per-request rounding in the docs. Is rounding applied per-request, per-batch, or at invoice aggregation time? Are there minimums or bucket sizes we should model (e.g., round up to nearest 10 tokens for discount tiers)?

5) Examples — can you provide 2–3 concrete billing examples we can plug into a spreadsheet?

Attached is a short set of example prompts and expected outputs (poc_prompt_examples.txt).

Appreciate a clear, example-based response — procurement wants a single-line "cost per request" for three common request shapes.

Thanks,
Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme-corp.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Token counting & rounding for hosted API — POC cost modeling

Tom / Sean / Monica — here are the concrete rules and three worked examples. I kept the math explicit so you can drop it into your model. Attachment: poc_token_examples.csv (CSV with the sample rows below).

High-level rules (hosted API):
- Input tokens = everything we send into the model in that API call: system prompt + user prompt + any injected context (e.g., session history supplied in the same request). Tool calls are not charged as part of that initial request unless the tool output is returned to Redwood in the same call.
- Tool outputs (from external services) are only billed when they are ingested by the model in a subsequent API call. If you call a tool and then send the tool response back as prompt/context in the next model invocation, the tokens in the tool response are counted as input tokens on that subsequent call.
- Model-generated tokens (model completions) are billed as output tokens. If you stream, we measure the final produced token stream for billing (not per-chunk), but streaming clients may see partial chunks earlier — we still bill only for the final produced tokens.
- Rounding and aggregation: we meter per-request exactly (token counts are integers). There is no coarse "round-to-10" at the request level; rounding happens only in invoice formatting where we present totals and apply currency rounding. In practice, that means you should model costs using exact token counts per request; small fractional-dollar noise will be adjusted at invoice time.

Attribution notes:
- When a function/tool is invoked via the model (model emits a function call), the tokens the model used to generate the func-call payload are charged as output tokens on that call. If you then feed the tool output back into a new call, those tool-output tokens are charged as input on that new call. We do not double-charge the tool output across the two separate invocations.
- If you use Redwood-hosted tools (private tool integrations that run inside Redwood's runtime), the tooling output may be included in the same billing window depending on how you configure the call; we'll mark those cases explicitly in the invoice breakdown.

Worked examples (all token counts are integers):

Example 1 — single-generation (no tools)\- System prompt: 30 tokens
- User prompt: 120 tokens
- Model completion: 240 tokens
Billing: Input = 30 + 120 = 150 tokens; Output = 240 tokens.
Cost line (example rate, hosted): $0.0008 per input token, $0.0015 per output token => (150 * 0.0008) + (240 * 0.0015) = $0.12 + $0.36 = $0.48 per request.

Example 2 — model triggers tool, tool output re-fed (two calls)\Call A (model -> tool):
- System prompt: 20 tokens (input)
- User prompt: 80 tokens (input)
- Model function call payload generated: 40 tokens (output)
Billing for Call A: Input = 100 tokens; Output = 40 tokens.

External tool returns 400-token result (not billed by Redwood yet). You then make Call B, sending the tool output back as context:
Call B (model consumes tool output):
- System prompt: 20 tokens
- Context including tool output: 400 tokens
- User follow-up prompt: 30 tokens
- Model completion: 120 tokens
Billing for Call B: Input = 20 + 400 + 30 = 450 tokens; Output = 120 tokens.

Total billing across flow: Input tokens = 100 + 450 = 550 tokens; Output tokens = 40 + 120 = 160 tokens.
Cost line: (550 * input_rate) + (160 * output_rate).

Example 3 — streaming long completion with intermittent tool calls\- Single call where user sends 200 tokens in total input (system + user). Model streams and produces 2,800 tokens over time, but you receive a tool call midway and then a short follow-up consume (tool output re-ingested later in the same session) — implementation detail: if the tool output is injected in a subsequent API call, it will be charged on that call. For the initial streaming request we bill the final produced 2,800 tokens as output (we do not sum per-chunk).

Rounding FAQ (short):
- We do NOT apply per-request coarse rounding (no round-up-to-5/10 token buckets).
- Tokens are integer counts; billing math multiplies by rates and invoices round currency to cents.
- Volume discounts and reserved capacity pricing apply at aggregation/contract level; the underlying metering remains per-request exact counts.

Other practical pointers:
- If you want predictable per-request pricing for procurement, consider using a small dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) or a commitment with a fixed monthly invoice; we can provide a blended "per-request" proxy price for modeling.
- We can provide a CSV (attached) with simulated traces if you share a representative sample of requests — that makes the POC costing exact.

Let me know if you'd like me to convert these three examples into a single-line per-request cost for each shape (I can compute with your target rates).

-Karthik
